title: Calculate linear magnification (lenses)

hook.scenario: Microscope mein lens lagakar dekhte hain toh bacteria 100 guna bada dikhta hai.
hook.question: Yeh 100x zoom ka number exactly kaise calculate hota hai?

mental_model.intuition: Mirror magnification jaisa hi hai, bas v/u formula ka minus sign gayab ho gaya.
mental_model.description: Lens mein bhi m = h'/h hota hai. Lekin distance wale formula mein m = +v/u hota hai (mirror mein -v/u tha). Agar m positive hai toh virtual/erect, aur negative hai toh real/inverted.

explanation:
Magnification (m) humein bataata hai ki image, object ke mukable kitni badi ya choti bani hai. Ratio form mein, iska formula hamesha m = h' / h hota hai (height of image divided by height of object).

Lenses ke case mein, magnification ko object distance (u) aur image distance (v) se link karne wala formula thoda sa badal jata hai. Mirrors mein hum m = -v/u use karte the. Lenses mein light us-paar nikal jati hai, aur formula ban jata hai m = v/u (without any negative sign in front).

Aap in dono ko mila kar ek useful equation bana sakte ho: m = h'/h = v/u. Numericals solve karte time yeh bahut kaam aata hai.

Sign of 'm' ka meaning bilkul mirror jaisa hi rehta hai. Agar m negative (-) hai, toh samajh lijiye height of image minus mein hai, yani image Inverted aur Real hai. Agar m positive (+) hai, toh image Erect aur Virtual hai.

Values ko dekhein toh: Agar m ki value (minus/plus ignore karke) 1 se zyada hai, toh image badi hai (Magnified). Agar 1 se choti hai (jaise 0.5), toh image choti (Diminished) bani hai.

key_points.title: Distance Ratio for Lenses
key_points.detail: m = v / u (Notice there is NO minus sign here, unlike mirrors).

key_points.title: Interpreting 'm'
key_points.detail: Negative m = Real & Inverted. Positive m = Virtual & Erect.

common_mistakes.title: Using -v/u for lenses
common_mistakes.explanation: Formula confusion is extremely common. Remember: Lens Formula has a minus (1/v - 1/u), so its Magnification has a plus (v/u). Mirror Formula has a plus (1/v + 1/u), so its Magnification has a minus (-v/u).
